summary: J. A. B. van Buitenen worked in Indology and philosophy, earning his PhD at Utrecht University (1946–1953) under Jan Gonda and Ali Beth. He held posts at Deccan College, Utrecht University, and the University of Chicago.

J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Colombo from around 1961 to 2002 and held an attested post at SOAS University of London in 1996.

J. C. Wright worked in Indology and linguistics and earned an MD from the University of London in 2007. He served as a professor at the University of London and as a specialist gynaecologist at Hamlin Fistula International in 2013.

J. Duncan M. Derrett was an Indologist who studied at Emanuel School, Jesus College, Oxford (~1940–1947), and SOAS University of London (~1947–1949). He held a post at the University of London from around 1949 to 1982.

J. F. Blakiston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Wellington College (~1896–1900). He served in the Archaeological Survey of India as assistant (1911), superintendent (1916), and Director-General (1935–1937).

J. G. Jennings was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. at the University of Oxford. He served as an English teacher and Principal at Muir Central College, and later as Director of Public Instruction for Bihar and Orissa.

Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara and Baylor University.
J. H. F. Hamilton was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Oxford from around 1877 to 1881. He served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service in 1879.

J. J. Johnson worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and Durham University. He served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society from around 1879 to 1912.

J. L. Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Bimal Krishna Matilal and at Rice University (~1968–1972). He served on the faculty at Victoria University of Wellington from around 1973 to 2018.
J. M. E. McTaggart was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College from around 1882 to 1885. He held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1897 to 1923.

J. N. Farquhar was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and Oxford, where he studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He later served as Wilde Lecturer at the University of Manchester (1927–1929).

Indologist and linguist J. N. Reuter studied at Helsinki, Jena, and Berlin under Otto Donner, Berthold Delbrück, and Albrecht Weber. He served as Acting Professor at the University of Helsinki from 1891 to 1931.

J. Nelson Fraser worked in Indology and other fields. He served as Professor of English Literature at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1896–1908) and as Principal of the Secondary Training College, Bombay (~1908–1918).

id: P:J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong
summary: J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong was a scholar of linguistics and other fields who studied at Leiden University from around 1905 to 1913. He subsequently held posts at Leiden University in 1922 and from 1935 to 1956.

J. P. Mallory is an archaeology and linguistics scholar who studied at Occidental, UCLA, UC Merced, UC Irvine, Rice, and Florida State. He held posts at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2011), UC Irvine, Rice, and Florida State.

J. P. Mills worked in Indology and other fields, having studied at Windlesham House School, Winchester College, and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served as a Reader at SOAS University of London from 1948 to 1955.
J. Peter L. Gwynn was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his education at St Columba's College, Trinity College, Hartford (~1934–1938), and University College London (~1938–1939).

J. Robert Oppenheimer studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, learning under Alfred North Whitehead and Arthur W. Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, Cambridge, the Manhattan Project (~1942–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~1947–1966).

J. S. Negi is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He was engaged in research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977) and served as Chief Editor at CIHTS (attested 1993–2001).
